_description: Where a run executes, as opposed to what it does. train_config.json holds the training values - agents, batch sizes, reward coefficients - and is identical on every machine. This file holds the two things that are not: how much hardware is available, and where the filesystem is. Resolved by train/runtime.py; the notebook selects a platform and a GPU toggle and reads everything else from here.
_note: Nothing here changes the learning problem. Moving a run between the sets below changes wall-clock time and output paths, not the trained policy (up to sampling nondeterminism). Values that would change the result belong in train_config.json.

hardware._note: Exactly two sets, selected by runtime.detect_hardware() from torch.cuda.is_available() and the notebook's USE_GPU toggle. The ceiling is 2 CPUs + 1 GPU (a Colab free VM, and what `docker run --gpus all` is assumed to get); the floor is 1 CPU + 0 GPUs. Both sets keep num_learners=0, so the learner runs in the driver process rather than a remote actor - a second process would cost one of the two CPUs and buy nothing at this model size. `ray_init` is passed to ray.init(); `train_config` overrides TrainConfig fields, and every key must name a real field or runtime.resolve() raises.

gpu._description: 2 CPUs + 1 GPU. Sampling is the bottleneck in this environment (Python order-book matching), so both CPUs sample in parallel while the in-process learner does the PPO update on the GPU. See doc/09 S5: `num_env_runners=N, num_learners=0` is the shape for a CPU-bound sampler.

cpu._description: 1 CPU, no GPU. One process does everything: no remote env runner, because there is no second core for it to run on, and a remote actor on the same core is pure IPC overhead. This is also the shape the test suite runs against.

ray_init_common._note: Merged into every profile's ray_init, so these are stated once rather than per set. Profile keys win on a collision.

platforms._note: Filesystem shape per machine. `repo_path` is where the package and config/ live; null means 'the working directory already is it', which is the case on Colab (the notebook must chdir there before it can read this file at all) and for a local checkout. `results_root` and `episode_data_root` replace TrainConfig.log_base_dir and .episode_data_dir; null leaves the configured value alone, which keeps it relative to the working directory. Splitting the two matters on Colab: checkpoints are small and must survive a disconnect, while the per-step episode record is ~34MB per 4096-step episode (measured at 8 agents) and has no business crossing the Drive FUSE layer. episode_sample_every and episode_max_bytes bound it; see the league_self_play group of train_config.json.

colab._description: Colab VM with Google Drive mounted. Checkpoints stay in the Drive-backed repo so a disconnect is recoverable with is_restore; episode pickles go to the VM's local disk and die with the session.
colab._pip_note: Read by the notebook's bootstrap cell, which runs before the package is importable and so reads this file with plain json.load. Pins must track requirements.txt. torch, numpy, pandas and scikit-learn are deliberately absent: Colab preinstalls them, and installing this repo's pins would replace Colab's CUDA torch build with a CPU wheel.

docker._description: The docker/ml/dockerfile_ray_torch image. The package is installed editable at /workspace/code, so outputs land in the repo - which is the host working tree when it is bind-mounted there, and otherwise the baked copy inside the container.

local._description: Any other machine: a dev checkout, or CI. Nothing is relocated, so paths behave exactly as they do for `python -m gym_continuousDoubleAuction.train.train`.
